For each prime \(p^k\), the number of ordered exponent pairs with max \(k\) is \((k+1)^2-k^2=2k+1\). Thus:
\[
(2\cdot 3+1)(2\cdot 1+1)(2\cdot 2+1)=7\cdot 3\cdot 5=105
\]
ordered pairs \((m,n)\).

Only \((m,n)=(600,600)\) has \(m=n\). So the number with \(m\le n\) is:
\[
\frac{105-1}{2}+1=53
\]

\boxed{53}
